q1: SELECT C.DEPT_NAME, AVG(I.SALARY) FROM COURSE AS C INNER JOIN DEPARTMENT AS D ON (C.DEPT_NAME = D.DEPT_NAME) INNER JOIN TEACHES AS T ON (C.COURSE_ID = T.COURSE_ID) INNER JOIN INSTRUCTOR AS I ON (D.DEPT_NAME = I.DEPT_NAME) GROUP BY C.DEPT_NAME HAVING AVG(I.SALARY) > 50000 AND COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) = 4

explanation: Q1 and Q2 differ in the COUNT(DISTINCT I.SALARY) condition of the HAVING clause. Q1 requires exactly 4 distinct salaries, while Q2 requires more than 4. This leads to different results when the count of distinct salaries is exactly 4.
counterexample_dsp: A department with exactly 4 distinct instructor salaries above 50000 average. Q1 returns it, Q2 does not.
